title: Name the pause.
old_caption:
When a fight gets too hot, it's okay to step away. Just say how long and that you're coming back.
Twenty minutes apart can save the whole conversation.

title: Curious first.
old_caption: It's tempting to walk into the make-up talk with your whole case ready. Try one question first: what was that like for you? Listening opens more doors than winning.

title: Retire "always".
old_caption: "You always" and "you never" turn one hard night into a trial. Name the moment and how it felt instead. Small and specific is so much easier to fix.

title: Say it back.
old_caption: Nodding while you load your reply isn't listening. Before you answer, say back what you heard and check you got it right. Feeling heard comes before fixing anything.

title: One fight at a time.
old_caption: A fight about the lights can turn into a fight about 2019 fast. Keep the old folders closed and solve tonight's thing together. Save this for the next tangle.

title: Swap "or" for "and".
old_caption: Holiday plans can feel like a contest someone has to lose. Try asking how you can do both, kindly. Planning side by side beats a tug of war every time.

title: Let the sorry land.
old_caption: Saying "it's fine" when it isn't keeps the hurt around. When someone apologises well, let it in: "thank you, I needed that." Receiving a sorry is part of the repair too.

title: The sorry is a start.
old_caption: Hearing the same sorry every week gets tiring. A sorry shows you see it; a small change shows you mean it. Pair the apology with one plan you can actually keep.

title: What's under it.
old_caption: Sometimes the dishes are just dishes, and sometimes they're carrying a bigger feeling. Gently ask what it's really about. The real thing is usually easier to solve together.

title: Move it off the screen.
old_caption: Late-night fights over text go sideways because tone doesn't come through. Ask to talk tomorrow, face to face. A short "ok." sounds very different with a smile attached.
